theme: wildcard: an airline network planner who knows capacity, schedule, far

candidates.name: openskynetwork/opensky-api
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Python/Java client for the OpenSky Network REST API: pulls current and historical ADS-B state vectors (aircraft position, altitude, velocity, callsign) and, via the OpenSky historical database (separate access tier), full flight tracks and airport arrival/departure counts back to ~2019. GPL-3.0, actively maintained (OAuth2 support added March 2026, 175 commits).
candidates.why_useful: Airport-level arrival/departure counts and general-aviation vs commercial traffic mix are a free, granular substitute for OAG/Cirium schedule data — a leading indicator of point-to-point leisure air capacity into Airbnb-heavy destination markets (addresses gap #10, airline capacity/traffic).
candidates.geography: Global (ADS-B receiver coverage-dependent; strong in US/EU, weak in parts of LatAm/APAC)
candidates.time_coverage: Real-time; historical DB back to ~2019 via OpenSky's academic/historical endpoint (separate quota)
candidates.size_hint: API, not a static dump; historical pulls can be large (state-vector granularity)
candidates.last_activity: 2026 (active, OAuth2 migration for March 2026 API change)

candidates.name: api-evangelist/opensky
candidates.what_it_holds: Independent third-party API profile of OpenSky Network: OpenAPI specs, JSON Schema, auth/rate-limit docs, pricing plans. Not the API itself and not data — pure documentation/spec artifacts. Created/modified 2026-06-13.
candidates.why_useful: Useful only as a faster on-ramp to understand OpenSky's REST/Trino surface before building a puller; no standalone data value beyond the official client above.

candidates.name: yashmasalge/Air_traffic_Passenger_Statistics
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed CSV (Air_Traffic_Passenger_Statistics.csv) of San Francisco International Airport's official open-data release: monthly passenger counts by airline, terminal, and geographic region (domestic/international), used here for a K-means clustering exercise. Small, single-airport, unclear date range (SFO's public portal version runs ~2005-present).
candidates.why_useful: SFO is a decent West-Coast leisure/business proxy and the source (SFO open data portal) also publishes similar CSVs for enplanements by region — a template for pulling comparable structured monthly airport traffic that could stand in for regional US travel demand feeding Airbnb NA nights.
candidates.time_coverage: Monthly, range unclear from repo (likely subset of SFO's 2005-present portal history)

candidates.name: zsszabo86/SatRday-Challenge
candidates.what_it_holds: Hungarian Central Statistical Office data on monthly passengers and available seats to/from Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport by origin country, 2007-2012, used for a ticket-sales-efficiency analysis.
candidates.why_useful: Old and narrow (pre-2013, one airport) but demonstrates a national-stats-office source (KSH) for scheduled seat capacity by origin country — a template for CEE regional air-capacity data that could flesh out EMEA regional mix; low direct value given the date range predates ABNB's operating history.

candidates.name: dchlseo/eia-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Lightweight Python utility wrapping the U.S. EIA API's /petroleum/pri/spt route. Currently implemented: Kerosene-type jet fuel spot price (EPJK) plus crude, diesel, heating oil, gasoline, propane — returns a tidy pandas DataFrame (date, product code/name, price, unit) with CSV export. 8 commits, license unspecified, recent (Sep 2026) activity.
candidates.why_useful: Jet fuel spot price is a fast-moving, freely available cost input to airfares; airfare inflation/deflation is a substitution variable for STR demand and a component of BLS CPI airfares already held — this is a lighter-weight, more current alternative puller than scraping EIA's own site directly, useful for a leading-indicator airfare-cost overlay on travel demand.
candidates.time_coverage: EIA API history (typically 1990s-present for petroleum spot prices)
candidates.size_hint: API wrapper, not a static dump
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps with FRED airfare/CPI series already held; adds jet-fuel-specific cost input not currently in the FRED panel

candidates.name: bhavanaeh/SkyScan
candidates.what_it_holds: Small real-time/historical flight-tracking web app built on the OpenSky Network API ("SkyScan USA"); wraps live and historical flight data but does not itself ship a stored dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Another thin OpenSky wrapper; marginal beyond the official client, included for completeness since it demonstrates a US-specific filtering pattern that could be reused for regional flight-density queries.

candidates.name: MiguelGonzalezAlvarez/Web-Flight-Delay-Tracker
candidates.what_it_holds: Real-time flight-delay prediction/tracking app for 35+ Spanish airports using OpenSky Network API live data plus an AI delay-risk model; no historical data files committed.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal; illustrates OpenSky filtering scoped to Spanish airports (useful if the team ever wants Spain-specific air-capacity context for the Barcelona Inside Airbnb market), but ships no data of its own.

notes: Session-wide WebSearch budget was exhausted before this scout could issue any web searches (all 200 calls used by other concurrent agents) — every query here ran through `gh search repos` only, verified via WebFetch on GitHub pages. gh also hit the shared 5,000/hr rate limit twice; one 40s sleep-and-retry recovered it, three queries (flight fare price history, cruise ship itinerary x2, DOT BTS T-100, digital nomad visa) never got a clean run and should be retried by the next agent once quota resets. Ten wildcard ideas, as an airline network planner would frame them, with hit/miss noted: (1) BTS T-100 / DOT segment-level air-carrier capacity by market pair — MISS on GitHub (no mirror found; likely because BTS publishes a clean bulk-download portal already, so nobody bothers hosting a copy — worth trying the BTS TranStats bulk CSV directly instead of GitHub); (2) OpenSky Network ADS-B historical flight tracks/airport arrival-departure counts — HIT (official client + several thin wrappers), a genuine free leading-indicator of air capacity into leisure markets, medium potential; (3) airport monthly passenger statistics (SFO, other US/EU open-data portals) — weak HIT, small single-airport CSVs only, no aggregator found; worth trying ACI World or FAA/Eurostat avia_paoc portal directly; (4) Amtrak/rail GTFS + ridership — MISS, no relevant repos surfaced (GTFS schedule repos exist broadly but none paired with ridership); (5) Google Flights / OTA historical fare scraping — could not search (rate-limited before running query fully); this is a well-known GitHub space (e.g. 'google-flights-scraper', 'skyscanner-python-sdk' style repos from memory) that the next agent should chase specifically, since airfare trend is a strong substitution/complement signal for STR demand; (6) rental car price/availability tracking (Kayak, Turo) — MISS, zero results, likely thin GitHub coverage of this niche; (7) cruise line itinerary/port-call capacity as a 'book-ahead' kernel analogue (gap #18, NCLH advance sales) — could not complete search (rate-limited), should be retried, and NCLH/RCL/CCL investor-relations advance-booking disclosures might be a better lead than port schedules; (8) EIA jet-fuel/petroleum spot price API wrapper — HIT (dchlseo/eia-data), low-but-real value as a cost-side overlay, complements the FRED airfare series already held; (9) consumer card-spending trackers (Opportunity Insights, Visa/Mastercard spend) — MISS via gh search text (Opportunity Insights' own repo is well-known from training data as 'OpportunityInsights/EconomicTracker' — the next agent should fetch that URL directly rather than keyword-search, since it is already a named gap-#6 target); (10) NYC TLC airport taxi trip data as an airport-arrivals volume proxy (also gap #10 explicitly) — MISS via gh search (TLC trip-record mirrors are common on GitHub from memory, e.g. 'toddwschneider/nyc-taxi-data', but text search on 'NYC TLC airport taxi trip data' returned nothing; try the exact known repo name directly). Overall: the airline/rail/road capacity angle is thinner on GitHub than expected — most of this data lives on clean government bulk-download portals (BTS TranStats, EIA, TLC) that nobody bothers mirroring to GitHub, so 'method' repos wrapping those APIs (like the EIA and OpenSky ones found here) are the more realistic yield than raw data dumps. Next scout should: (a) retry the rate-limited queries (flight fares, cruise itineraries, BTS T-100, digital nomad visas) fresh; (b) go straight to known-from-training repo names (OpportunityInsights/EconomicTracker, toddwschneider/nyc-taxi-data, openflights/openflights schedule data, skyscanner APIs) via WebFetch rather than keyword search, since gh's full-text search misses well-known repos whose README doesn't literally contain the query phrase; (c) check if WebSearch budget has reset before spending more gh calls.
